sections.title: Cash Flow, Land Investment & Balance Sheet
sections.subtitle: Reported FCF swings on land-premium timing, not operating performance -- read it as a multi-year average, not a single period

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Reported FCF swung from RMB-17.9bn (FY2022) to RMB+42.2bn (FY2024) purely on land-premium timing; the DCF does not use FCF/WACC on this stream, it capitalises attributable earnings instead.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities (owners' share only; NCI equity of ~RMB34bn sits inside total liabilities’ complement, not here); plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For COLI: most of the asset base is RMB442bn of property inventory at cost and RMB203bn of investment property at fair value. Book is accreting (+4.3%/yr over 5 years) even as earnings power has fallen 70%, which is the core tension this valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • Inventory impairments against the carrying value of land and projects
  • Liabilities growing faster than equity

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total interest-bearing debt (bank loans + bonds; lease liabilities and amounts due to NCI shareholders are excluded).

For COLI: net gearing (net debt / equity, company definition) is ~27%, moderate for a Chinese developer, funded at a blended 2.76% cost of debt. The DCF's capitalised-earnings stream is already post-interest, so it sets net_debt to zero rather than deduct it twice.

What to watch:

  • Net gearing trend versus peers mid-downturn
  • Refinancing dates on the bond book

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in RMB major units.

For COLI: the dividend was cut from HK121c (FY2021) to HK50c (FY2025) even as land spend rose -- the payout ratio has been defended at roughly 40% of a shrinking EPS, not held at a fixed cents figure.

What to watch:

  • EPS 5-year CAGR of -22%: the collapse in earnings power behind the valuation's earnings leg
  • Whether a further dividend cut tracks EPS or gets defended out of cash

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure.

For COLI: FCF is dominated by land-premium timing, not operating performance -- it swung from RMB-17.9bn (FY2022, heavy land buying) to RMB+42.2bn (FY2024, land spend pulled back). The DCF deliberately does not discount this series; it capitalises attributable earnings at the cost of equity instead and treats reported FCF as noise.

What to watch:

  • A multi-year average, never a single period, of FCF
  • Whether land spend is being deferred (inflating FCF) rather than genuinely reduced

ipAdditions.title: Investment property additions vs CapEx
ipAdditions.content:
Investment property additions is cash spent growing the held-for-rent/REIT-recyclable portfolio (offices, malls, business parks) at fair value; CapEx captures the rest of the fixed-asset spend.

For COLI: the bull case leans on recycling part of the RMB203bn investment-property book through REITs or disposals to help close the 0.32x price-to-book gap; this chart is the lead indicator for whether the portfolio the company could recycle is still growing or being run down. Additions fell from a RMB11.9bn FY2020 peak to the RMB4-7bn range FY2023-25 as the sector contracted.

What to watch:

  • Additions trending toward zero (de-risking) versus a renewed ramp (fresh commitment)
  • Occupancy of the existing portfolio (78% at the latest interim) alongside any further build

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest, tax and NCI.

For COLI: gross margin has fallen from ~30% (FY2020) to 15.5% (FY2025) as low-margin land bought at the top of the cycle is handed over; ROE has fallen from 14% to roughly 3% over the same period. This margin collapse, not revenue, is why attributable earnings have compounded at -22%/yr.

What to watch:

  • Whether margin stabilises as high-cost legacy land works through, or keeps falling on fresh low-margin sales
  • Net margin drag from NCI leakage on JV-heavy projects

profitNci.title: Profit attributable to owners vs incl. NCI
profitNci.content:
Profit attributable to owners is net income after minority interests; profit incl. NCI is total consolidated profit before that split.

For COLI: the gap is profit earned by joint-venture/project partners on consolidated projects, not by COLI's own shareholders. That leakage rose sharply -- NCI's share of profit was 5.5% in FY2025 and 12.2% at the H1 FY2026 interim -- as NCI equity grew to RMB34bn. The DCF's earnings stream is already net of this, so a widening gap here is a real cost to the valuation, not an accounting artefact.

What to watch:

  • NCI's share of profit continuing to widen as tier-1 JV projects dominate handovers
  • NCI equity growing faster than attributable equity

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is recognised on handover of completed units plus investment-property rental income.

For COLI: handovers lag contracted sales by 1.5-2 years, so today's revenue reflects sales made in a much worse market; the base case assumes further declines of roughly -8%/-2% before stabilising. Revenue is down -2%/yr over both 3 and 5 years -- a shrinking but not collapsing top line, unlike earnings.

What to watch:

  • Contracted sales today as the leading indicator for revenue 1.5-2 years out
  • Mix shift toward investment-property rental income as development slows
